fixed.before: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Out of the love with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved me more than all the beings on high, He made me a garment of majesty in which every kind of light is set, and wrapped me in it; and He made me a royal crown in which are set forty-nine stones that burn with the light of the orb of the sun, whose radiance goes into the four [quarters of] the firmament Aravot, into the seven firmaments and into the four winds of the world; and He bound it on my head and called me the Lesser YHWH before all His household on high, as it is said, For My name is within him. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Out of the great love and great compassion with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved and cherished me more than all the beings on high, He wrote with His finger, with a pen of flame, on the crown that is on my head, the letters by which heaven and earth were created, the letters by which seas and rivers were created, the letters by which mountains and hills were created, the letters by which stars and constellations, lightnings, wind and thunders, thunderclaps, snow, hail, storm and tempest were created, the letters by which the needs of the world and all the secrets of creation were created; and each and every letter shines, face within face, like the appearance of the going forth of the sun, and the moon and the stars. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, bound this crown on my head, all the princes of kingdoms in the height of Aravot and all the armies of every firmament trembled before me; and even the princes of the *elim* [mighty ones], the princes of the *tafsarim* [officers] and the princes of the *erelim* [an angelic order], who are greater than all the ministering angels who serve before the throne of glory, trembled and shook before me; and even Samael the wicked, the head of all the adversaries, who is great in all the kingdoms on high, feared and quaked; and even the angel of fire, the angel of hail, the angel of wind, the angel of lightning, the angel of wrath, the angel of thunder, the angel of snow, the angel of rain, the angel of the day, the angel of the night, the angel of the stars and the constellations, who guide the whole world by their hands, tremble and shake before me when they see me. And these are the names of the princes who guide the world: Gabriel, the angel of fire; Baradiel, the angel of hail; Ruhiel, the angel who is appointed over the wind; Barakiel, the angel who is appointed over the lightnings; Za'amiel, who is appointed over wrath; Zikiel, who is appointed over the sparks; Zu'iel, who is appointed over the tremors; Za'afiel, who is appointed over the raging storm; Ra'amiel, who is appointed over the thunders; Ra'ashiel, who is appointed over the earthquake; Shalgiel, who is appointed over the snow; Matariel, who is appointed over the rain; Shimshiel, who is appointed over the day; Leliel, who is appointed over the night; Galgalliel, who is appointed over the orb of the sun; Ofanniel, who is appointed over the wheel of the moon; Kokhaviel, who is appointed over the stars; Rahatiel, who is appointed over the constellations. And all of them fall on their faces when they see me, and cannot gaze at me because of the majesty and splendour, the radiance, brilliance, beauty, comeliness, brightness and light of glory that are on my head. Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, the Prince of the Presence, the splendour of the height of all, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, took me to serve the throne of glory and the wheels of the chariot and all the needs of the Shekhinah, at once my flesh was turned to flame, my sinews to fire, my bones to coals of broom, the light of my eyelids to the brilliance of the firmament, the balls of my eyes to torches of fire, the hair of my head to blaze and flame, all my limbs to wings of burning fire, and the body of my stature to blazing fire. On my right are hewers of flames of fire, on my left a torch of fire burns, and around me blows a wind of tempest and storm, and the noise of quake upon quake, before me and behind me.

fixed.before: The *parha* of sorb trees: *shedim*. A sorb tree that is close to a town has no fewer than sixty *shedim*. What practical difference does it make? For writing an amulet for it.
fixed.after: It flew away. Those of the sorb trees are *shedim*. A sorb tree that is close to a town has no fewer than sixty *shedim*. What practical difference does it make? For writing an amulet for it.

fixed.before: פרחא/פרחי (111b.4-6) is an unidentified tree or shrub; at 111b.6 the syntax of פרחא דבי זרדתא is unclear. רישפי 'fiery spirits' is uncertain. 111b.5: לגזוזי 'dodging' is uncertain. 111b.7: בר קשא 'town official' is uncertain (perhaps a town elder or strongman); 'does not know Blessed' presumably means he cannot even say a blessing. 111b.8: כנפיא 'wings' is obscure; some read it as 'like a sieve'.
fixed.after: פרחא/פרחי (111b.4-6) is an unidentified tree or shrub; at 111b.6 פרחא is taken as 'it flew away', ending the story, and דבי זרדתא שידי begins the next statement, as in 111b.4. רישפי 'fiery spirits' is uncertain. 111b.5: לגזוזי 'dodging' is uncertain. 111b.7: בר קשא 'town official' is uncertain (perhaps a town elder or strongman); 'does not know Blessed' presumably means he cannot even say a blessing. 111b.8: כנפיא 'wings' is obscure; some read it as 'like a sieve'.

not_upheld.h2#1: אסור לספר הימנו is the idiom 'it is forbidden to converse with him', the usual reading of Shabbat 75a.
not_upheld.h2#2: Agrat, Azlat, Asya, Belusya are read as four names in the incantation, the usual reading; 'Agrat has departed' is an alternative, not a correction.
